(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Icrypex]] | years6 = 2021–2022 | team6 = [[Basket Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] | years7 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team7 = [[Wisconsin Herd]] | years8 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team8 = [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] | years9 = 2023–2024 | team9 = [[Vanoli Cremona]] | years10 = 2025 | team10 = [[Hapoel Holon]] | years11 = 2025–2026 | team11 = [[Hapoel Galil Elyon]] | years12 = 2026–present | team12 = [[Fundación Lucentum Baloncesto|HLA Alicante]] | highlights = *Second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2019) }} '''Jordan Latham Bone''' (born November 5, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Fundación Lucentum Baloncesto|HLA Alicante]] of the Spanish [[Primera FEB]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]].{{Cite web |title=Jordan Bone - Men's Basketball |url=https://utsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jordan-bone/6744 |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=University of Tennessee Athletics |language=en}} ==High school career== Bone attended [[The Ensworth School]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]], where he played for the private high school's varsity basketball team.{{cite web | last=Ramey | first=Grant | title=Ensworth's Jordan Bone leans on his brother, a former Vol | website=The Tennessean | date=2016-06-06 | url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/ut/2016/06/05/ensworths-jordan-bone-leans-his-brother-former-vol/85467538/ | access-date=2024-12-31}} He was teammates with NBA player [[James Wiseman]].{{Cite web |last=Bossi |first=Eric |date=December 5, 2015 |title=Wiseman, Bone impress in Nashville |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/wiseman-bone-impress-in-nashville |access-date=April 21, 2019 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]}} He was ranked by [[247Sports]] as the 171st overall prospect in his class. ==College career== As a freshman playing for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|University of Tennessee]], Bone averaged 7.2 points and 2.9 assists per game, only to improve on those averages as a sophomore with 7.3 points and 3.5 assists. As a junior, Bone had a breakout season, posting 13.5 points, 5.8 assists, and 3.2 rebounds per game and helping Tennessee to secure a 31–6 season as well as to make a Sweet 16 appearance.{{Cite news |last=Daniels |first=Ivan |date=April 3, 2019 |title=Tennessee star guard Jordan Bone declares for NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Jordan-Bone-Tennessee-NBA-Draft-130836008/ |access-date=April 9, 2019 |work=247 Sports}} He was named to the Second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]]. At season's end, he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] and forfeited his remaining year of eligibility.{{Cite news |date=April 3, 2019 |title=Tennessee's Jordan Bone says he's entering NBA draft |url=http://www.startribune.com/tennessee-s-jordan-bone-says-he-s-entering-nba-draft/508064422/ |access-date=April 9, 2019 |work=Star Tribune |agency=Associated Press}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2019–2020)=== Bone was selected in the second round with the 57th overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], who later traded him to the [[Detroit Pistons]] via the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Draft Rights To De'Andre Hunter, Solomon Hill And Conditional 2023 Second-Round Pick From New Orleans |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-draft-rights-to-deandre-hunter-solomon-hill-conditional-2023-pick-from-pelicans |access-date=July 6, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Draft Rights To Bruno Fernando From 76ers |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-draft-rights-bruno-fernando-76ers |access-date=July 6, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |date=July 8, 2019 |title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Jordan Bone In Draft Night Trade With Philadelphia |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-jordan-bone-draft-night-trade-philadelphia |access-date=July 9, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} On July 8, 2019, Bone signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pistons. He will split playing time between the Pistons and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Grand Rapids Drive]].{{Cite web |date=July 8, 2019 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Jordan Bone To Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-jordan-bone-two-way-contract |access-date=July 8, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} Bone scored 22 points against the [[Memphis Hustle]] on December 26, 2019, but suffered a knee injury and missed a game.{{Cite news |date=December 27, 2019 |title=Pistons' Jordan Bone: Out again Saturday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-jordan-bone-out-again-saturday/ |access-date=January 11, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]]}} ===Orlando Magic (2020–2021)=== On November 27, 2020, Bone signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |date=November 27, 2020 |title=Orlando Magic Sign Five |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jordan-bone-karim-mane-devin-cannady-robert-franks-jon-teske-20201127 |access-date=November 28, 2020 |website=NBA.com}} On February 3, 2021, the [[Orlando Magic]] announced that they had waived Bone.{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2021 |title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Frank Mason III to Two-Way Contract Orlando waives Jordan Bone |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-frank-mason-two-way-contract-20210203 |access-date=February 3, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} ===Delaware Blue Coats (2021)=== On February 6, 2021, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] announced that they had acquired Bone and a 2021–22 third-round pick from the [[Lakeland Magic]] in exchange for the returning player right to [[J.P. Macura]], the returning player right to [[Doral Moore]] and a 2021–22 second-round pick.{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2021 |title=Blue Coats Acquire Jordan Bone from Lakeland Magic |url=https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-acquire-jordan-bone-from-lakeland-magic |access-date=February 6, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} He made his debut for the Blue Coats on February 11, 2021. ===Beşiktaş (2021)=== On August 23, 2021, Bone signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Icrypex]] of the [[Basketball Super League|Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2021 |title=Jordan Bone Beşiktaş Icrypex'te |url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/81539/jordan-bone-besiktas-icrypexte.html |access-date=August 23, 2021 |publisher=Beşiktaş |language=tr}} He averaged 11.7 points, 3.6 assists, and 3.6 rebounds per game in 11 games. ===Basket Zaragoza (2021–2022)=== On December 9, 2021, Bone signed with [[Basket Zaragoza]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web |last=Yahyabeyoglu |first=Fersu |date=December 9, 2021 |title=Jordan Bone (ex Besiktas) signs at Zaragoza |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/720511/Jordan-Bone-(ex-Besiktas)-signs-at-Zaragoza |access-date=December 9, 2021 |website=Eurobasket}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2022–2023)=== On November 3, 2022, Bone was named to the opening night roster for the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2022 |title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2022–23 Opening Day Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2022-23-opening-day-roster/n-5895537 |access-date=November 3, 2022 |website=oursportscentral.com}} ===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2023)=== On February 24, 2023, Bone was traded to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] in exchange for [[Deividas Sirvydis]].{{Cite web |last=East 19, 2023 |website=VanoliBasket.it |language=Italian}} On February 27, 2026, he signed for [[Fundación Lucentum Baloncesto|HLA Alicante]] of the Spanish [[Primera FEB]].{{Cite web |date=February 27,
